articles.title: The father and son on opposite sides of Alberta’s separation vote
articles.summary: Albertans are voting on whether to stay in Canada or pursue independence via a referendum, splitting even some close-knit families.
articles.body:
On Monday, people in Alberta will cast their ballots in a vote that includes a question on whether the western province should remain in Canada or pursue a binding provincial referendum on separation.

The other questions on the ballot paper ask Albertans about options to gain more autonomy from Ottawa, including on matters such as immigration control and access to social services for non-permanent residents.

In the separation vote, the remain side is expected to win, but the debate has caused tensions in Alberta. The BBC’s Nadine Yousif travelled to Buck Lake to speak with the close-knit Pietsch family, who have a father and son on either side of the debate.

articles.title: Fears for bats in Gwynedd's Bluebell Woods if glamping pods approved
articles.summary: Without a mitigation strategy the effect on the creatures would be "major", a survey says.
articles.body:
Fears have been raised over plans for a glamping site in a woodland with multiple species of bat.

Gwynedd council was considering the application for 11 pods at Bluebell Woods, Caerhun, which would also include pathways, a parking area, soft landscaping and drainage.

A bat survey commissioned before the proposed work concluded that without a mitigation strategy the impact on the creatures would be "major" and restrict many of "the most light-sensitive species" from continuing to use the location.

It is an offence to kill, injure, take or disturb a bat, or to destroy, damage, obstruct or otherwise interfere with a bat roost, breeding site or resting place.

Several species of bat were identified on the proposed site, including the common and soprano pipistrelle, as well as the myotis bat.

They were observed entering the woodland from the north of the site and along the road corridors in the area, as well as "congregating" in the open parkland in the south-west corner.

The mitigation strategy recommendations included "maintaining the woodland as a suitable flight corridor and foraging area", to preserve part of the woodland as a "dark area for bats".

Without mitigation, the impact would be assessed "as major" at a national level, primarily due to the effect of lighting on bat access through the woodland, the survey said.

Further ecological mitigation proposed included use of bat boxes, a lighting plan with "properly positioned and shielded lighting minimising light spill", standard trees and 20 smaller trees and hedging.

articles.title: VÍDEO: Casal bebe e conversa em bar em meio a atos violentos em Paris  | G1
articles.standfirst: Sébastien Lecornu pediu que cidades imponham toque de recolher já na noite de segunda-feira (19). França enfrenta série de distúrbios, saques e edifícios incendiados em atos violentos após manifestações pacíficas de estudantes.
articles.summary: Sébastien Lecornu pediu que cidades imponham toque de recolher já na noite de segunda-feira (19). França enfrenta série de distúrbios, saques e edifícios incendiados em atos violentos após manifestações pacíficas de estudantes.
articles.body:
Um casal foi visto bebendo e conversando em meio a distúrbios violentos em Paris. Imagens registraram o homem e a mulher em um bar perto do Arco do Triunfo, na região onde vêm ocorrendo os principais distúrbios no centro da capital francesa ( veja acima ).

No vídeo, chamas de uma lixeira em chamas podiam ser vistas ao fundo, enquanto o homem e a mulher estavam sentados na mesa de um café.

➡️ A França vem enfrentando nas últimas semanas uma onda de manifestação que começaram a partir protestos estudantis e ganharam apoio de manifestantes contra a alta no custo de vida e no preço dos combustíveis . Nos últimos dias, no entanto, alguns atos ficaram violentos, com saques, prédios incendiados e confrontos com a polícia. No sábado (17), 2.400 pessoas foram detidas.

A onda inicial de protestos começou no mês passado em escolas de ensino médio nos subúrbios pobres ao norte de Paris e focavam na indignação com a ausência de professores e as instalações precárias em escolas. Rapidamente, as manifestações se transforaram em um movimento nacional contra a desigualdade, a insuficiência de gastos públicos e a queda na qualidade dos serviços.

Os protestos ocorrem ainda no momento em que o presidente Emmanuel Macron entra na reta final de seu mandato, deixando para trás um eleitorado polarizado e um cenário político interno fragmentado .

Nesta segunda-feira (19), o primeiro-ministro da França, Sébastien Lecornu, solicitou a prefeitos de cidades com manifestações que decretem toques de recolher por conta dos protestos . Lecornu, que divide o govenro da França Macron, quer que as cidades imponham a restrições já na noite desta segunda .

"Pedi aos prefeitos que decretassem vários toques de recolher nesta noite, toques de recolher parciais", disse Lecornu.

O primeiro-ministro não especificou para qual cidades solicitou o toque de recolher. Ele conduziu uma reunião de emergência para decidir medidas a serem tomadas para controlar a violência nas ruas.

Também nesta segunda, o Museu do Louvre, em Paris, amanheceu fechado após manifestantes bloquearem o acesso ao local em apoio ao movimento estudantil e para denunciar "a repressão policial".

Na madrugada de domingo (18), o país registrou uma das noites mais violentas dos últimos anos. Segundo o Ministério do Interior, mais de 500 mil pessoas foram às ruas em dezenas de cidades. Os atos deixaram um morto, mais de 500 policiais feridos e quase 1.800 detidos.

Homem caminha diante de fogo em meio a manifestação em Paris, em 18 de outubro de 2026. — Foto: Abdul Saboor/ Reuters

articles.title: Corpo de segundo jovem que desapareceu no Rio Grande é encontrado | G1
articles.standfirst: Pedro da Silva Firmino, de 17 anos, desapareceu na madrugada de sábado (17), após tentar salvar o amigo, que também morreu. A caminhonete que eles estavam afundou no rio e apenas uma pessoa sobreviveu.
articles.summary: Pedro da Silva Firmino, de 17 anos, desapareceu na madrugada de sábado (17), após tentar salvar o amigo, que também morreu.
articles.body:
Caminhonete retirada do Rio Pardo após acidente em Colômbia, SP — Foto: Kelven Melo/EPTV

O corpo de Pedro da Silva Firmino, de 17 anos, foi encontrado na manhã desta segunda-feira (19), dois dias após a caminhonete em que ele estava afundar no Rio Grande, em Colômbia (SP).

O amigo dele, Tiago Henrique de Matos Silva, de 23, foi localizado sem vida na tarde de domingo (18) . Ele estava perto de uma ponte, segundo a Defesa Civil.

O terceiro ocupante do veículo, Lucas Torquato de Morais, de 21, foi o único sobrevivente. Ele se agarrou a uma bomba de captação de água e conseguiu sair do rio.

Ao g1 , Lucas disse no domingo que Pedro mergulhou para tentar salvar Tiago, que era levado pela correnteza. O acidente aconteceu na madrugada de sábado (17). (veja vídeo abaixo)

Os jovens, que são de Indaiatuba (SP), estavam em Colômbia para passar o fim de semana e foram passear pela Orla Municipal.

Segundo a Defesa Civil, Tiago, que dirigia a caminhonete, não identificou o fim do trecho asfaltado, o que fez com que a caminhonete entrasse no rio por um embarcadouro de canoas.

Ainda segundo as autoridades, todos conseguiram sair do veículo, mas Tiago e Pedro foram arrastados pela correnteza.

Pescadores fazem buscas por jovens desaparecidos no Rio Grande, em Colômbia, SP — Foto: Reprodução/Defesa Civil

Segundo Lucas, os três voltavam para a pousada onde estavam hospedados depois de passear pela cidade . Eles acharam que a rua contornava o rio, mas o veículo caiu na água.

Em nota divulgada no sábado, a Defesa Civil do Estado de São Paulo informou que o motorista não identificou o fim do trecho asfaltado. Por isso, a caminhonete entrou no rio por um embarcadouro de canoas na Orla Municipal.

Os três conseguiram sair da caminhonete, mas foram arrastados pela correnteza. Lucas, que não sabe nadar, se agarrou a uma bomba de captação de água.

Segundo ele, Tiago foi levado pela correnteza, e Pedro tirou o sapato e o boné e mergulhou atrás do amigo, chegando a alcançá-lo. Lucas acompanhou os dois pela margem até perdê-los de vista.

"É uma coisa muito ruim a gente estar tendo que dar um depoimento desse. Eu queria que a gente tivesse nós três aqui falando isso".

articles.title: Noruega quer proibir plataformas de jogo aos menores de 16 anos | G1
articles.standfirst: Proposta também prevê restrições a jogos como Roblox e aplicativos de mensagens considerados nocivos; projeto de lei deve ser apresentado até o fim do ano.
articles.summary: Proposta também prevê restrições a jogos como Roblox e aplicativos de mensagens considerados nocivos; projeto de lei deve ser apresentado até o fim do ano.
articles.body:
Europa quer proibir uso de plataformas digitais por menores de 13 anos — Foto: Jornal Nacional/ Reprodução

O governo da Noruega anunciou nesta segunda-feira (19) que pretende incluir alguns jogos e plataformas de mensagens em seu projeto de proibição de redes sociais para menores de 16 anos .

Oslo, que deve apresentar um projeto de lei sobre o tema até o fim do ano, modificou sua proposta para incluir as "plataformas nocivas".

São consideradas "nocivas" as redes ou plataformas que, "por seu design, suas características ou seus conteúdos, representam um risco para o desenvolvimento emocional, cognitivo ou para a saúde das crianças, ou para sua segurança", afirmou o governo em um comunicado.

Aplicativos como TikTok, Snapchat e o jogo Roblox , em seu estado atual, também deverão enfrentar restrições.

"Hoje existem certas plataformas que se apresentam como jogos, mas que na verdade estão repletas de recursos como sistemas de recomendação algorítmica e publicidade ilegal direcionada às crianças", disse a ministra da Infância e da Família, Lene Vagslid.

"É por isso que queremos que elas também sejam incluídas", afirmou ao canal público de televisão NRK.

O limite de idade será válido até 1º de janeiro do ano em que a criança completar 16 anos . As plataformas deverão implementar, por conta própria, um sistema de verificação de idade.

O governo trabalhista tem minoria no Parlamento, o que significa que precisará obter o apoio de outras legendas para aprovar a lei.

A Austrália instituiu no ano passado uma legislação que proíbe menores de 16 anos de acessar determinadas redes sociais, enquanto a União Europeia prevê, por sua vez, adotar restrições "graduais", com diferentes níveis segundo a idade.

articles.title: Quem era a família que morreu após carro colidir contra carnaúba no PI | G1
articles.standfirst: A professora Érika Oliveira trabalhava em duas escolas de Campo Maior. O filho dela, Alberto Felipe, era atleta mirim de jiu-jítsu, e a sobrinha, Isabella Damasceno, fazia aulas de capoeira.
articles.summary: Érika Oliveira atuava em duas escolas do município. O filho dela, Alberto Felipe, era atleta mirim de jiu-jítsu, e a sobrinha, Isabella Damasceno, fazia aulas de capoeira.
articles.body:
Quatro pessoas da mesma família morreram após um acidente de carro na PI-215 , entre os municípios de Campo Maior e Coivaras , no Centro-Norte do Piauí, na tarde de domingo (18). As vítimas foram identificadas como as crianças Alberto Felipe Paz Oliveira e Isabella Damasceno Ribeiro, a professora Érika Oliveira e Francisco de Assis Oliveira. Todos eram da mesma família

Outra criança da família ficou ferida e permanece internada. Em nota, a Prefeitura de Campo Maior lamentou as mortes e informou que Érika Oliveira era esposa de Francisco de Assis, mãe de Alberto Felipe e tia de Isabella Damasceno.

Segundo a prefeitura, Érika atuava como professora no Centro Municipal de Educação Infantil Tia Medeiros e na Escola Municipal Vida Verde. Já Alberto se destacava como atleta mirim de jiu-jítsu. Isabella, por sua vez, era aluna de capoeira e era conhecida no esporte pelo apelido de "Estrela Cadente".

"A perda de Érika, de Isabella, do esposo e do filho da professora causa profunda contestação e deixa de luto familiares, amigos, colegas de trabalho e toda a comunidade escolar do município", afirmou a prefeitura.

O Centro de Treinamento Eduardo Oliveira, onde Alberto praticava jiu-jítsu, cancelou as atividades desta segunda-feira (19) em sinal de luto pela morte do aluno.

O presidente da Câmara Municipal de Campo Maior, Wellington Sena, também lamentou a morte das vítimas e afirmou que a tragédia abalou toda a cidade.

"Quatro rostos, quatro histórias, duas delas que mal começaram a ser escritas. E uma tragédia que abalou profundamente a nossa Campo Maior. Hoje, todos nós vamos dormir mais tristes. Amanhã, amanheceremos mais reflexivos, com o coração apertado e a certeza de que a vida é frágil e preciosa", afirmou.

Taxista morre após mal súbito durante partida de futebol no Piauí; 'deixou uma ausência muito grande', diz esposa — Foto: Reprodução/Redes Sociais

Informações repassadas ao g1 pela Polícia Militar de Campo Maior apontam que o motorista viajava com a mulher e três crianças quando, por motivos ainda desconhecidos, perdeu o controle do veículo e colidiu violentamente contra uma carnaúba às margens da rodovia.

Quatro ocupantes morreram no local após a colisão. Com a força da batida, o carro pegou fogo. Pessoas que passavam pela rodovia retiraram as vítimas fatais e a criança sobrevivente do veículo antes que as chamas se espalhassem.

O Serviço de Atendimento Móvel de Urgência (Samu) foi acionado e encaminhou a criança para o Hospital Regional de Campo Maior. O estado de saúde dela não foi informado.

A Prefeitura Municipal de Campo Maior manifesta profundo pesa pelo falecimento de quatro pessoas da mesma família, vítimas de trágico acidente, entre elas a professora Érika Oliveira, que atua no Centro Municipal de Educação Infantil Tia Medeiros e na Escola Municipal Vida Verde, e sua sobrinha, a aluna Isabella Damasceno Ribeiro, da Escola Municipal Dr. Nonato Ibiapina.

A perda de Érika, de Isabella, do esposo e do filho da professora causa profunda consternação e deixa de luto familiares, amigos, colegas de trabalho e toda a comunidade escolar do município.

Neste momento de imensa dor, a Prefeitura de Campo Maior se solidariza com todos os familiares e amigos, bem como com os profissionais da educação e estudantes das unidades escolares atingidas por essa tragédia.

Que Deus conceda conforto, força e serenidade a todos para enfrentar essa perda irreparável.

É com profundo pesar que comunicamos o falecimento de nosso atleta mirim, Alberto Filipe P. O., e de seus familiares, vitimas de um trágico acidente ocorrido na tarde deste domingo, entre Campo Maior e a localidade de Coivaras.

Apenas sua irmã sobreviveu, mas encontra-se em estado muito grave no hospital. Neste momento de imensa dor, nos solidarizamos com todos os familiares, amigos e pessoas próximas, desejando força e conforto para enfrentar essa perda irreparável.

Em respeito a esse momento de luto, comunicamos o cancelamento de todas as nossas atividades nesta segunda-feira.

Que Deus receba aqueles que partiram em um bom lugar e conforte os corações de todos os familiares e amigos. Que Ele conceda força e amparo a todos neste momento tão difícil.

Wellington Sena, presidente da Câmara de Vereadores

Quatro rostos, quatro histórias, duas delas que mal começaram a ser escritas. E uma tragédia que abalou profundamente a nossa Campo Maior.

Hoje, todos nós vamos dormir mais tristes. Amanhã, amanheceremos mais reflexivos, com o coração apertado e a certeza de que a vida é frágil e preciosa.

Diante de uma dor tão imensa, faltam palavras para expressar a tristeza e a solidariedade às famílias que enfrentam essa perda irreparável.

Que Deus abençoe nossa cidade, conforte os corações dos familiares e amigos e dê força a todos os campomaiorenses para atravessar este momento de luto.

A Abadá Capoeira Campo Maior lamenta profundamente a precoce partida da nossa querida aluna Estrela Cadente.

Sua presença, seu sorriso e sua alegria deixarão saudades em todos que tiveram o privilégio de compartilhar momentos ao seu lado. Hoje, nossa família da capoeira se une em oração, solidariedade e carinho, diante dessa perda tão dolorosa.

Que Deus, em sua infinita bondade, conforte os corações de seus familiares e amigos, concedendo-lhes força, fé e serenidade para enfrentar este momento de imensa tristeza.

Estrela Cadente, sua luz continuará brilhando em nossas lembranças e em nossos corações.

Com profundo pesar, Abadá Capoeira Campo Maior.

* Vitória Bacelar, estagiária sob supervisão de Ilanna Serena.

articles.title: Dia do Servidor em Sergipe: ponto facultativo muda para 30 de outubro | G1
articles.standfirst: Expediente nas repartições públicas será normal no dia 28; serviços essenciais continuam funcionamento sem interrupção.
articles.summary: O Governo de Sergipe transferiu o ponto facultativo do Dia do Servidor para 30 de outubro, mantendo o expediente normal nas repartições estaduais no dia 28.
articles.body:
Palácio Governador Augusto Franco em Sergipe. — Foto: Ascom

O Governo de Sergipe transferiu a comemoração do Dia do Servidor Público Estadual, celebrado em 28 de outubro, para a sexta-feira (30). A alteração foi publicada no Diário Oficial do Estado nesta segunda-feira (19), por meio do Decreto nº 1.584.

Com a medida, o expediente nas repartições públicas estaduais funcionará normalmente na quarta-feira (28). O ponto facultativo será aplicado na sexta-feira (30).

De acordo com o texto do decreto, os serviços essenciais, a exemplo de atendimento na área da saúde e operações de segurança pública, vão funcionar sem interrupção.

A alteração no calendário administrativo do estado entrou em vigor na data de sua publicação.

Na semana passada, a Prefeitura de Aracaju já havia informado a mesma alteração para os servidores municipais.

articles.title: Fumaça em Manaus: 559 atendimentos de saúde registrados em outubro | G1
articles.standfirst: Os sintomas mais frequentes relatados pelas pessoas que procuraram as unidades de saúde foram tosse, falta de ar, dor de cabeça, febre, dor torácica, coriza, irritação na garganta, fadiga, mal-estar e náusea.
articles.summary: Fumaça em Manaus causou 559 atendimentos de saúde em outubro, com relatos de tosse e falta de ar devido ao aumento das queimadas no Amazonas.
articles.body:
Atendimento em unidade de saúde de Manaus — Foto: Douglas Santos / SES-AM

A rede estadual de saúde atendeu 559 pessoas em Manaus , entre 1º e 17 de outubro , por problemas relacionados à fumaça que atinge a capital e municípios da Região Metropolitana. Os dados são da Fundação de Vigilância em Saúde do Amazonas – Dra. Rosemary Costa Pinto (FVS-RCP).

Segundo o órgão, 92 pacientes foram atendidos no sábado (17), um dos dias mais intensos de fumaça na região. No dia, a concentração de partículas finas de poluição chegou a 59,2 vezes o valor recomendado pela Organização Mundial da Saúde (OMS) para a média anual desse poluente, segundo a plataforma internacional IQAir.

Entre os sintomas mais relatados pelos pacientes estão tosse, falta de ar, dor de cabeça, febre, dor no peito, coriza, irritação na garganta, cansaço, mal-estar e náusea.

A Secretaria de Estado de Saúde do Amazonas (SES-AM) orienta a população a evitar a exposição prolongada à fumaça. A pasta também recomenda reduzir as atividades físicas ao ar livre nos períodos de maior concentração de poluentes, manter os ambientes fechados e beber água com frequência.

Crianças, idosos, gestantes e pessoas com doenças respiratórias ou cardiovasculares devem redobrar os cuidados.

Os atendimentos ocorreram em meio ao aumento dos incêndios no Amazonas. Segundo dados do Painel do Fogo, o estado registrou 1.892 focos de calor entre 1º e 17 de outubro de 2026, alta de mais de 190% em relação ao mesmo período de 2025.

Do total registrado em outubro, 1.641 focos de calor foram identificados em áreas públicas e 120 em áreas privadas. Outros 133 ocorreram em locais sem identificação da propriedade, segundo o Painel do Fogo.

Em assentamentos federais, o número de focos de calor no período é de 320, enquanto 124 foram identificados em unidades de conservação. Em terras indígenas, o índice é de 124 focos. Sem classificação, o índice chegou a 1297 focos.

Piora na qualidade do ar causada por fumaça

Em pouco mais de um mês, Manaus teve mais de 20 episódios de fumaça provocada por incêndios florestais.

O problema, registrado pela primeira vez em 8 de setembro, se agravou em outubro, quando a capital passou nove dias consecutivos com fumaça no ar, aulas foram suspensas, atividades ao ar livre foram canceladas e centenas de pessoas procuraram atendimento médico por problemas relacionados à poluição.

A fumaça que encobriu a capital vem de incêndios registrados na Região Metropolitana de Manaus e em municípios do interior do Amazonas. O avanço das chamas é favorecido pela vegetação seca, pela baixa umidade e pelas altas temperaturas, em um cenário associado aos efeitos do fenômeno climático El Niño. A ação humana, responsável por iniciar grande parte dos incêndios, também contribui para agravar a situação.

Medidas anunciadas para reduzir impactos

As medidas incluem a criação de um Estado-Maior Conjunto para coordenar a atuação das Forças Armadas e dos órgãos envolvidos no combate aos incêndios florestais, que avançam no estado e provocam fumaça em Manaus.

O anúncio foi feito durante uma coletiva de imprensa na sede da Superintendência da Zona Franca de Manaus (Suframa), na capital, após uma reunião entre representantes dos governos federal e estadual. Segundo o ministro da Defesa, José Múcio Monteiro, a nova estrutura de comando começou a atuar neste domingo e deve agilizar a tomada de decisões e a mobilização dos recursos.

articles.standfirst: No local, foram encontradas uma garrafa com álcool e uma caixa de fósforos. Companheiro não estava no apartamento na hora do incêndio.
articles.summary: Após incendiar o próprio apartamento em Vitória para tentar matar o namorado, Alessandra dos Santos Silva foi detida com álcool e fósforos no bairro de Lourdes.
articles.body:
Uma mulher foi presa após atear fogo no apartamento onde mora no bairro de Lourdes, em Vitória , na noite deste domingo (18). Alessandra dos Santos Silva, de 40 anos, confessou ter incendiado o quarto para tentar matar o namorado que ela pensava estar lá dentro.

Segundo informações da Guarda Municipal, os agentes foram acionados para atender uma ocorrência de violência doméstica em um local onde já havia registro anterior. Ao chegarem lá, foi constatada fumaça preta saindo de uma das janelas.

Questionada sobre a situação, Alessandra informou que seu namorado estaria no quarto que estava em chamas. Os agentes quebraram a parede, combateram o incêndio e constataram que o homem não estava no local.

Alessandra confirmou ter ateado fogo no quarto acreditando que o companheiro estivesse lá dentro. No apartamento, foram encontradas uma garrafa com álcool e uma caixa de fósforos.

Alessandra foi levada para a Delegacia Regional de Vitória. Segundo apuração da TV Gazeta, ela foi presa em flagrante por incêndio e levada ao sistema prisional.

articles.title: VÍDEOS mostram saques em lojas na França e desespero de comerciantes | G1
articles.standfirst: Testemunhas registraram cenas que revoltaram as redes sociais em vídeos que viralizaram: um homem sendo agredido pelas costas após confrontar os manifestantes, uma mulher tentando apelar para a razão e o choro de um lojista que perdeu tudo.
articles.summary: Testemunhas registraram cenas que revoltaram as redes sociais em vídeos que viralizaram, como um homem sendo agredido pelas costas após confrontar os manifestantes.
articles.body:
Vídeos que viralizaram nas redes sociais mostram o desespero de comerciantes e a tentativa de evitar a destruição completa de suas lojas durante o dia intenso de protestos que a França viveu no sábado (17).

Um deles mostra o dono de uma franquia da maior rede de varejo de videogames e cultura pop da França , a Micromania, em Nice, tentando proteger a porta de sua loja com o próprio corpo. Em determinado momento, ao ser confrontado por um dos jovens, ele anda em direção a ele e, ao virar de costas, é atacado com um chute e lançado no chão com força.

Outro vídeo mostra uma mulher que ainda tentou se colocar na frente dos manifestantes e apelar para a razão. Nas imagens, ela questiona o porquê deles estarem fazendo aquilo e diz que os saques não fazem parte da causa que os protestos estão defendendo.

Apesar da tentativa, ela não é ouvida e um dos manifestantes, que não participava do ato de vandalismo, a afasta e pede:

"Você vai se machucar. Eles não vão ouvir a razão".

Um terceiro vídeo mostra um comerciante após o ataque à sua loja. Sentado na fachada, ele chora ao ver a destruição total do local.

"Vocês talvez tenham destruído o único meio de vida dele", criticou a pessoa que filmou a cena na legenda.

No domingo (18), os protestos continuaram, mas em menor escala . Na porta de um supermercado em Paris, o dono fez um desabafo que também foi registrado em vídeo e postado nas redes.

"Olha só, que vergonha! Não é possível. Existe forma e boas maneiras para fazer exigências, mas não assim. O que fizemos para vocês? Somos homens de família. É o nosso maldito supermercado! Como vamos sobreviver agora? Estou atrasado com o seguro. É para mim que vocês estão trazendo suas exigências?", questionou.

À agência de notícias Reuters, Gerard Nouchi, gerente de duas lojas de roupas de Marselha que foram saqueadas, relembrou o que viveu:

"No sábado, fomos saqueados por jovens dos bairros, provavelmente dos distritos do norte. Eram muitos, pelo menos 5 ou 6 mil pessoas. Eles destruíram tudo, quebraram coisas, nos insultaram. Foi como um verdadeiro tornado, com o pano de fundo de uma polícia nacional com efetivo insuficiente. Criminosos prosperam quando pessoas honestas estão ausentes".

Cenas que viralizaram nas redes sociais de saques em lojas da França — Foto: X /Reprodução

➡️ A França vem enfrentando nas últimas semanas uma onda de manifestação que começaram a partir protestos estudantis e ganharam apoio de sindicatos e de manifestantes contra a alta no custo de vida e no preço dos combustíveis. Nos últimos dias, no entanto, alguns atos ficaram violentos, com saques, prédios incendiados e confrontos com a polícia. No sábado (17), 2.400 pessoas foram detidas.

A onda inicial de protestos começou no mês passado em escolas de ensino médio nos subúrbios pobres ao norte de Paris e focava na indignação com a ausência de professores e nas instalações precárias das escolas.

Rapidamente, as manifestações se transforaram em um movimento nacional contra a desigualdade, a insuficiência de gastos públicos e a queda na qualidade dos serviços.

Os protestos ocorrem no momento em que o presidente Emmanuel Macron entra na reta final de seu mandato, deixando para trás um eleitorado polarizado e um cenário político interno fragmentado.

articles.title: Estiagem no oeste do Pará: Mojuí decreta emergência e Belterra age | G1
articles.standfirst: Falta de chuvas afeta 3,1 mil moradores da zona rural em Mojuí dos Campos. Município vizinho se antecipa contra seca severa e risco de queimadas.
articles.summary: A estiagem no oeste do Pará deixou 3,1 mil pessoas sem água em Mojuí dos Campos, enquanto Belterra prepara ações contra a seca e queimadas florestais.
articles.body:
Nível da água baixa e expõe solo com troncos secos em área de manancial no oeste do Pará. — Foto: Reprodução/Portal do Carpê

A estiagem no oeste do Pará levou a Prefeitura de Mojuí dos Campos a decretar situação de emergência na zona rural nesta segunda-feira (19), após o desabastecimento de água atingir diretamente 3,1 mil pessoas. No município vizinho de Belterra, a administração municipal aprovou um plano de contingência para estruturar o combate à seca e conter o avanço de queimadas florestais na região.

Em Mojuí dos Campos, o Decreto nº 370 foi publicado no Diário Oficial dos Municípios com prazo de vigência de até 180 dias. O documento aponta que o esgotamento de fontes naturais e a redução na vazão de poços artesianos comprometeram o acesso à água potável, deixando riachos, nascentes e pequenas barragens completamente secos.

Além das dificuldades para o consumo humano e animal, a escassez hídrica provocou perdas na agricultura e nas pastagens de produtores rurais locais. Com o reconhecimento do nível II de emergência, os órgãos municipais passam a atuar sob coordenação da Defesa Civil, que planeja convocar voluntários e arrecadar recursos para amparar as comunidades.

Em Belterra, a prefeitura publicou o Decreto nº 145 para colocar em vigor o Plano de Contingência Municipal de Proteção e Defesa Civil (Plancon) para o período 2026/2027. O instrumento busca organizar ações preventivas contra a estiagem severa e incêndios em áreas de vegetação, cenário recorrente que motivou decretos de emergência na cidade em 2023, 2024 e 2025.

O planejamento municipal tomou como base relatórios técnicos do Serviço Geológico do Brasil (SGB), que identificaram 126 moradores em situação de risco crítico direto. Os trabalhos serão conduzidos pela Coordenadoria Municipal de Proteção e Defesa Civil, com monitoramento contínuo das previsões climáticas sobre o impacto de um possível fenômeno Super El Niño na Amazônia.

articles.title: Rugeley mum's cold sore warning after baby who contracted HSV dies
articles.summary: Ben Brookes and Meg Edmonds want to raise awareness of HSV after losing their daughter.
articles.body:
A bereaved mother whose newborn daughter died after contracting the herpes simplex virus (HSV) is urging other parents to learn about the little-known dangers cold sores can pose to babies.

For most adults, cold sores are usually a painful but common infection. But in newborn babies, whose immune systems are not yet fully developed, HSV can cause a life-threatening illness.

Meg Edmonds' daughter Magnolia died aged just 10 days in February and it is suspected the virus may have been passed on by her mother.

"The guilt is obviously unbearable, it's horrific, but I just try and remind myself that I didn't know and I did what I could have done with the knowledge that I did have," she said.

Warning: This story contains distressing details

She has decided to speak publicly as part of an infection prevention campaign run by the Lullaby Trust, a charity which promotes infant health.

The 22-year-old, from Rugeley in Staffordshire, said Magnolia was born healthy after what she described as a straightforward birth.

"I had a lovely birth with her, a water birth. She was nearly two weeks overdue like her big sister but everything was fine and she was born perfectly healthy," she said.

Only later did she realise she appeared to have a sore on her lip at around the time Magnolia was born.

"Looking back at photos now, I can see that I had a lesion or sore on my lip whilst I was giving birth which I thought nothing of at the time," Meg said.

"I had never had a cold sore or anything before.

"I'd asked health professionals if they thought it was a cold sore, but I was reassured that it wasn't, it was nothing to worry about.

"They just thought that I might need to drink more or that it might just have been hormonal from giving birth only the day prior, so I thought nothing of it."

But Magnolia's condition deteriorated and she later died from HSV.

The experience left Meg living with what she described as a constant reminder of her loss.

It was the first cold sore she had experienced, but another outbreak since Magnolia's death brought back painful memories.

"I'm now going to get them for the rest of my life, however regular that might be," she said.

"It's horrible. I was really dreading it because I'm constantly reminded anyway that my daughter isn't here any more and why that is, but to actually have a physical reminder on my face is horrible."

She said one of the hardest things to accept was that she had never realised a cold sore could pose a danger to a newborn baby.

"I'd heard of herpes before, but I'd only heard of it as the sexually transmitted infection," Meg said.

"I'd never heard that a cold sore could be the herpes virus and that the herpes virus could be so dangerous to a newborn baby."

The family had already taken precautions to protect Magnolia from infection.

"We chose not to have family round who were poorly at the time because I knew that was not safe," Meg said.

"But I'd never ever seen anything about cold sores, HSV, neonatal herpes, nothing, and it's only since that I've found so much out that I just wish I'd known before."

Meg said she never kissed her daughter and was careful about hygiene because Magnolia had been born during winter.

"I washed my hands constantly because I was worried in general about infections.

"But I never knew that if that passed to her it could kill her."

Research by the Lullaby Trust has highlighted the pressure some parents feel when asking people not to kiss or touch their baby.

"We know that parents can feel awkward, embarrassed or even guilty about asking someone not to kiss their baby, wash their hands or keep their distance when they're unwell," chief executive Jenny Ward said.

"But protecting your baby from infection is never something you need to justify."

She said the charity's THANKS advice - think hands and no kisses - was designed to help families reduce the risk of infection.

"Wash your hands before touching your baby and don't kiss them if you are unwell," she said.

"Viruses are really common, particularly at this time of year, and while we can't avoid them all we can put some steps in place to reduce the chance of your baby getting unwell."

articles.title: Council rejects phasing out plastics in Kingston Cemetery
articles.summary: Kingston Council says it must balance protecting the cemetery with the needs of bereaved families.
articles.body:
A south London council has rejected calls to phase out plastics in one of its cemeteries, despite concerns that they are creating a "massive environmental issue".

Ecologist Alison Fure petitioned Kingston Council to better enforce the ban on plastic decorative items at Kingston Cemetery, including ornaments, artificial flowers, pots, windmills and cellophane wrappers. It was signed by more than 1,200 people.

In a statement Fure said she hoped the cemetery could be restored to a "more natural and respectful environment".

Council leader Andreas Kirsch said the council would work with volunteers on the issue, but said it had to balance protecting the cemetery with the needs of bereaved families.

Fure, who has lived within walking distance of the cemetery in south-west London for 35 years, previously told BBC London that said environmental degradation caused by plastics had left the burial ground's ecology "hanging by a thread".

She said a change in policy would bring the site in line with other cemeteries in London.

In her petition, Fure said the accumulation of plastic both detracted from the "serenity of the grounds" and created "a massive environmental issue".

It was discussed at a council meeting on 13 October, during which the council heard that the cemetery, which is a Grade I Site of Importance for Nature Conservation (SINC), was littered with plastic decorations.

Fure told the meeting that plastic items gradually broke down into microplastics, which stayed in the environment and polluted the neighbouring Hogsmill River.

A report by council officers responding to the petition said the authority's focus was on collaboration rather than formally enforcing the ban on plastics at the cemetery, according to the Local Democracy Reporting Service .

Its current regulations restrict plastic fencing and visitors are asked to remove cellophane wrappers from flowers.

The council said it was prioritising an educational campaign to encourage visitors to stick to the rules.

The report said staff were told to remove plastic and cellophane wrappers from flowers during routine maintenance and carry out litter picks in the cemetery twice a week.

Independent councillor James Giles, submitted a motion for the council to agree to a phased withdrawal of plastic decorations at the cemetery over three months.

It was rejected with 33 votes against, two in favour and three abstentions.

articles.title: A British man who moved to Sweden in 2017 says officials told him no action was needed after Brexit; nine years later, the 60-year-old and his wife are hiding in a caravan as he fights a deportation order
articles.summary: At 51, he moved to Sweden with his wife in the hope for a better life; at 60, he is being asked to return to Britain.
articles.body: At 51, he moved to Sweden with his wife in the hope for a better life; at 60, he is being asked to return to Britain. With authorities on his back and no option in the future, Mark Smith has been forced into hiding alongside his wife Petra due to fears he will be deported as a result of what he says is a government Brexit residency error, as per a report by The Guardian.Smith, who has had heart attacks, strokes, severe headaches and chronically high blood pressure, was told on the phone that he should leave Sweden by October 17, as he was an "alien" without permission to stay. Terrified of deportation, he and his wife moved out of their home in Falkenberg, in south-west Sweden, to a caravan park. "We are in hiding; we daren’t go back to our apartment. We are scared to go out as we don’t know if the police will come and take us," Smith said.A court ruled on October 12 that a decision on deportation would not be suspended but gave him until October 20 to "submit his application for a retrial" in relation to "the grounds for the decision on indefinite deportation."It was back in 2017 that he moved to Sweden. At the time, Smith was told by the authorities that he did not need to do anything to stay after Brexit in 2020. He had a job, private health insurance, and was registered on the population register administered by the national tax authority, as required under Swedish rules.However, he was unaware that Sweden was among 13 of the 27 EU member states that required Britons living in the country before Brexit to make a formal application to remain. “I asked the tax authorities three times on different occasions if I had to do anything because of Brexit and they said no, telling me I had to wait for five years to apply for permanent residency," he told The Guardian. “Because it was the tax authority, a government body, I took it for granted that what they told me was correct,” he added.It was in 2021 that Smith's troubles began, when he started to get ill and applied for sickness benefit. He was then told by the officials that he should have applied for post-Brexit residency. The couple did so immediately at the end of 2021, with the deadline being 31 December. They waited for two years to hear back and when they did, it was only to get a rejection on the grounds that they were not married and therefore did not have a family connection to merit his residency in Sweden.Having lived together since 2017, the couple tied the knot in 2023. “We were so much in love; we lived together, we did everything together, even now we hold hands walking down the streets. We wanted to get married, we wanted to do it the right way. I wanted to ask Petra’s father for permission and have him give her away, but two weeks after he gave me permission to marry his daughter, he passed. So we were looking into marriage but things just kept happening. But we don’t understand why this matters,” said Smith. Family connections are not a criterion under free movement rights, which apply to any individual regardless of marital status, so campaigners believe they have a strong case.The couple also said they had not been given the full court paperwork from the first case appealing against the migration agency's decision, so they appealed to a higher court without the full arguments against them. After speaking to a judge, Petra has had assurances that all the paperwork will be sent to them by post, but they feel angry that they were not apprised of the information that the migration agency was arguing before the courts.According to David Milstead, a British-Swedish volunteer citizens' rights activist working with Brits in Sweden group, Smith's case was typical of many Britons living in Sweden. “Mark’s experience is far from unusual. I have encountered many British citizens who actively sought information from the Swedish authorities about their residence rights after Brexit, only to receive vague, unhelpful answers, sometimes being told that they needed to do nothing,” he shared with the outlet.Milstead said Smith’s case was “depressingly familiar” and should warrant the urgent attention of the European Commission, which has previously said Sweden was not breaking any laws. “A gentleman with Mark’s serious health conditions should not be having to fight deportation. It is difficult to understand how the European Commission has concluded that Sweden’s treatment of late applications under the [Brexit] withdrawal agreement does not warrant a challenge,” he said.According to Petra, Smith's health conditions have left him so vulnerable that she is not sure "if he will last until Christmas." “He has been told he can’t drive, he can’t fly – what do they expect him to do? Get up and walk to England? Come on, Sweden, we need to step back from all of this and be better,” she said.After 12 years with Smith, she said deportation would be devastating for her and her 15-year-old son with special needs, whom Smith co-parents. “It is wrong what they are doing; I feel ashamed to be Swedish. What they are doing is racist to British people,” Petra said.78-year-old widow Joyce Thomas, whose husband also inquired about Brexit residency and was told by the tax authorities there was nothing to do, is fighting a removal order. Previously, Sweden has deported 458 Britons, including one man who had been in the country since he was 10 years old, and a 65-year-old man married to a Swede with no family or property in the UK. The country also issued removal orders to a man with dementia who is in 24-hour care and has been in the country for 25 years. The Scandinavian country has found itself under mounting pressure over its approach to the withdrawal agreements having deported 458 Britons.Under the legally binding treaty, it was agreed governments would communicate Brexit residency rules, consider late applications on reasonable grounds and exercise "proportionate" decisions including in the case of vulnerable people. Sweden’s migration agency has said there is no evidence Sweden has taken an extreme approach to the withdrawal agreement.The UK Foreign Office has raised concerns about Sweden’s approach to the withdrawal agreement with the European Commission on numerous occasions, but has been told Sweden is not breaching the agreement. “We are in touch with Mr Smith and are providing consular support. We know this is a distressing and challenging time for those concerned and we are urgently raising the situation with both the Swedish authorities and the European Commission,” said a spokesperson.The Foreign Office welcomed a statement by Sweden’s former migration minister Johan Forssell in August that Sweden would examine “additional measures” that would address the issue of Brexit deportation, and a similar declaration by Magdalena Andersson, who is on track to form the new government.You use AI every day. articles.title: Floating book fair's maiden visit 'a huge homecoming for us'
articles.summary: A visit by Logos Hope to Manx waters next month marks the start of a new journey for one family.
articles.body:
A family from the Isle of Man is returning home after spending five years at sea aboard the world's largest floating book fair.

Andy Sheath, his wife Rebecca and daughters Elsie and Sofie have lived on the Logos Hope since 2021.

The vessel, which is due to dock in Douglas Harbour between 6 and 22 November, is home to more than 300 people from 60 countries and travels the world as the largest floating book fair.

Sheath said he had always hoped the ship would visit the island and was looking forward to finally coming home.

Sheath first visited the ship as a university student in 2010 and said he was the only Manxman on board.

He said stepping on to the vessel for the first time felt like coming home.

Since 2021, the ship has been the family's home and holds "precious, treasured memories", he said.

"My oldest daughter Elsie is five. These corridors echo memories of her first steps.

"Our table and dining room is where we've eaten for five years. It's where my daughters have grown from baby to toddler, to now," he said.

The family returned to the island for Sofie's birth, meaning Elsie remembers visits to the wildlife park, fish and chips on the beach with her grandparents and ice cream at Peel.

Sheath said his family is excited to return to the island to start a new life, calling it "a huge homecoming".

And fellow crew members have shared in the family's excitement about this stop on the boat's tour.

"They have asked me 'what can I do on the island', 'can we see the TT route?' and many other questions," Sheath said.

Sheath said he hoped the visit would not be the last from the Logos Hope.

"On the next visit I would love to see another Manx person on board," he said.

"I have proudly waved the three legs of Man at every port and I would love to see more Manx people waving the flag on board at different ports."

articles.title: World Food Programme forced to cut aid to Gaza due to funding shortages
articles.summary: The number of people helped by the UN agency in the Palestinian territory will drop by about a third - from 1.6 million to 1.1 million.
articles.body:
One of the main suppliers of food aid to the Gaza Strip, the World Food Programme (WFP), says that it is being forced to "drastically reduce lifesaving assistance" to the Palestinian territory due to funding shortages.

Overall, the number of people helped by the UN agency will drop by about a third - from 1.6 million to 1.1 million.

The cuts will hit as winter approaches and at a time when many families in Gaza are still struggling to feed themselves.

One effect is that the number of hot meals that are currently being provided by community kitchens will be cut from 250,000 to 150,000 each day.

Families living in hard-to-reach areas, for example near the so-called Yellow Line, which demarcates Israel's area of military control, will receive a meal every other day instead of daily.

Nearly all of Gaza's 2.1 million population remains displaced and two-thirds rely on food aid to survive.

"It's a disaster! What will we do with these reduced rations? How will we provide for the little ones?" said Mervat al-Satari, a displaced Palestinian mother-of-five at a camp in the al-Mawasi area of Khan Younis after being told of the WFP's news. "Sometimes we wait for these meals to eat."

"This will affect us a lot. The daily aid was somehow ticking the box but now it will be every two days," said Sawsan Bahloul, who is also from al-Mawasi and is a mother of three. She added that the portions given by the community kitchen - usually pasta or lentils with occasional potatoes and aubergines - were already too small to feed her family.

The Palestine director for the WFP, Shaun Hughes, is clear that the cuts are being made because of finances, and "not because the needs are coming down, or because we don't have access - we do."

Already, since July, there have been reductions in cash transfers provided to some half a million people, meaning they have less money to buy food in local markets. The number of Gazans given bags of flour and ration boxes by the WFP will now fall from 1.1 million to 600,000 each month.

The WFP received less than half as much funding for its Palestinian operations in 2026 as in previous years. The agency says it urgently needs $450m (£338m) to maintain "critical" operations over the next six months.

Despite a ceasefire between Hamas and Israel that was agreed a year ago, violence has continued, including almost daily Israeli strikes, and humanitarian conditions in Gaza remain dire.

There has been no reconstruction and little recovery, with Israel tightly controlling the entry of goods through crossings. While food markets are now well stocked, few can afford to buy from them. More than 80% of people in Gaza are unemployed so most of the population relies on aid.

Families currently receiving the WFP food handouts complained to the BBC that already these were insufficient and gave them little diversity in their diets.

"The flour isn't enough and the food boxes aren't enough either," said Dalal al-Dahdouh, who is living in the ruins of her home in Gaza City with her family of eight. She fears the new cuts will have "a major impact".

The mother draws a contrast between the current desperate situation and life before the war. "In the past, thank God, we had our own home and a wonderful life. We had fresh vegetables, proper sanitation facilities and our own land," she said. "Now we live entirely on aid, including WFP vouchers."

There is no cooking gas available in Gaza because the Israeli government considers it a "dual use" item that could be used by Hamas for military purposes. Wood is expensive, so many families send their children into the street to find plastic and cardboard to burn as fuel to make bread or heat food.

"It's still a very concerning humanitarian situation, people living in brutal conditions, most people still without a proper home, living in tents, poor access to water and sanitation and healthcare," Hughes of the WFP told the BBC. "Cuts to food assistance are going to compound that hardship that families have been facing for three years now."

Humanitarian workers say that despite a modest improvement in Gaza compared to a year ago, acute food insecurity and the risk of famine returning continue to loom over the territory.

In July, the Integrated Phase Classification (IPC) - the world's foremost experts on food security - reported that two-thirds of the population - 1.4 million people - were "expected to face crisis or worse levels of acute food insecurity in July-December 2026".

For now, the WFP says it can continue supporting bakeries that provide one-third of Gaza's bread needs and provide nutritional assistance to about 300,000 women and children. It also delivers health food snacks to some 200,000 children.

In the occupied West Bank, the WFP is continuing to give assistance to some 200,000 Palestinians, having halved the number of recipients in September.

The agency says food insecurity is rising in the territory mostly due to increased Israeli settler violence and Palestinian displacement.

articles.title: Austrian Airlines flight from Tel Aviv diverts to Bulgaria after ‘threat’
articles.summary: An Austrian Airlines flight from Tel Aviv carrying 57 people was diverted to the Bulgarian capital, Sofia, late on Sunday after a threat was made against the aircraft, an airline spokesperson told Reuters.
articles.body: VIENNA — A bomb threat forced an Austrian Airlines flight carrying 57 people from Tel Aviv to Vienna to divert to the Bulgarian capital, Sofia, late on Sunday, though a search found no danger, the airline and Bulgaria’s BTA news agency said. “We confirm that there was a threat against flight OS82 on October 18, 2026, from Tel Aviv to Vienna (TLV to VIE), which made it necessary for the flight to make an intermediate landing in Sofia (SOF),” the airline said in a statement Monday. “During the search of the affected aircraft, the passengers, and the crew, no danger was identified,” it said, adding that the flight continued from Sofia to Vienna with all passengers after reboarding. BTA said the flight’s crew reported receiving a bomb threat when the aircraft was approaching the Romanian border, and the Bulgarian Air Force scrambled MiG-29 fighter jets. The Lufthansa Group, which owns Austrian Airlines, Vienna Airport and the Austrian interior ministry did not respond to requests for comment. The Austrian and Bulgarian interior ministers were due to hold a previously scheduled news conference in Vienna later on Monday at 11 a.m. local time (5 a.m. ET). The incident came less than three weeks after a co-pilot on an Israel-bound flydubai jet allegedly attacked the captain with an ax in an attempt to crash the plane. The UAE attorney general said last week that an Omani flydubai co-pilot had intended to seize the Sept. 30 Dubai-Tel Aviv flight and crash it into a terminal at Israel’s Ben Gurion Airport in a suicide attack, before he was thwarted by the captain.

articles.title: Bike dumped in Andheri. Then a train to Delhi: How 3 accused in Tiger Shroff case were nabbed
articles.summary: MUMBAI: The Anti-Gangster Task Force and Rajasthan Police have nabbed three men in connection with the firing incident targeting actor Tiger Shroff’s car
articles.body: MUMBAI: The Anti-Gangster Task Force and Rajasthan Police have nabbed three men in connection with the firing incident targeting actor Tiger Shroff’s car in Mumbai.The accused, who were allegedly absconding, were apprehended from a train at Kota railway station in Rajasthan while travelling from Mumbai towards Delhi.Two of the accused are from Haryana, while the third is from Bihar and was living in Mumbai, according to the details of the arrested men.The accused have been identified as a minor, a resident of Sonipat district in Haryana; Hrithik Kumar alias Roshan, 22, who works as a Rapido rider and was living in Andheri West, Mumbai; and a Rehan, 18, a resident of Sonipat district in Haryana.Also read: ‘We have 70,000 shooters’: In 2nd audio gangster Anil Pandit vows to make Salman Khan’s life ‘hell’Meanwhile, security has been tightened outside actor Salman Khan’s residence at Galaxy Apartments in Mumbai’s Bandra area following the firing incident. Police personnel wearing bulletproof jackets and police vehicles were seen deployed outside the actor’s residence.According to police, unidentified assailants opened fire at Tiger’s car at around 7pm on Sunday as he was leaving a football club in Juhu. While the actor escaped direct gunshot injuries, his driver sustained injuries in the incident.Deputy Commissioner of Police Mohit Garg confirmed that the actor’s vehicle was targeted as he was leaving the club premises.The Mumbai Police Crime Branch had expanded its search operation to Gujarat to trace the suspects. According to sources, the accused had allegedly tracked Tiger’s movements and knew about his regular Sunday visits to the football ground.Investigators suspect the attackers conducted a recce of the area and familiarised themselves with the actor’s routine before carrying out the shooting.Sources said the suspects allegedly fled along SV Road, passing through Vile Parle and Andheri after the firing. They reportedly abandoned their motorcycle near Andheri West railway station before boarding a train towards Borivali. Investigators suspected they subsequently crossed into Gujarat to evade the police.Three to four Mumbai Crime Branch teams were conducting raids at suspected locations to trace and apprehend the accused.Meanwhile, Maharashtra Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde visited Tiger’s residence on Sunday night following the incident. He said the actor sustained injuries to his left hand from gunpowder and glass fragments. Shinde added that Tiger and his mother, Ayesha Shroff, were shaken by the incident and assured them of the state government’s support.“Strict action will be taken, and threats against public figures will not be tolerated,” Shinde said.An FIR was registered against three unidentified persons in connection with the shooting. articles.title: France protests live: PM wants some cities to impose ‘curfews’ after unrest
articles.summary: PM Sebastien Lecornu says he has asked regional authorities to impose ‘partial’ and ‘localised’ curfews in some cities.
articles.body:
French Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu says he has asked regional authorities to impose “partial” and “localised” curfews in some cities to protect businesses after weekend demonstrations spilled over into some of the worst street violence in recent years.

President Emmanuel Macron acknowledges “failures in anticipation and intelligence” but rules out the resignation of Interior Minister Laurent Nunez who admitted police “lost control” during days of violent protests mainly over the cost-of-living crisis.

articles.title: France’s Macron declines minister’s resignation after violent protests
articles.summary: Interior Minister Laurent Nunez acknowledges that police ‘lost control’ during weekend protests.
articles.body:
French ⁠President ⁠Emmanuel Macron has declined Interior Minister Laurent Nunez’s offer to resign ⁠after nationwide demonstrations by students protesting educational conditions and groups angry over the high cost of living turned into widespread riots and looting, the Elysee presidential office says.

Macron said Nunez should stay in his position to ensure the chain of command is maintained within the police and security forces and asked the interior minister ⁠to establish new methods to deal with looters, the Elysee said in a statement on ⁠Monday.

The president also asked Nunez to “take all necessary steps to ensure transparency over the failures in planning and intelligence that led to the violence”, the statement added.

The Ministry of the Interior said more than 2,300 people were arrested and almost 1,000 police and gendarmes injured in protests on Saturday. Injuries were also reported among protesters, with one demonstrator’s hand blown off by a police crowd-control grenade.

The nationwide demonstrations brought together students demanding better conditions in the French education system and residents protesting against the high cost of living and faltering public services.

More than half a million people took part in the protests on Saturday. Looting, arson and damage to property occurred in many cities, with masked rioters attacking town halls, police stations and other government buildings.

Nunez acknowledged on Monday that police “lost control” during the protests.

“On Saturday in some major cities, you couldn’t look shopkeepers in the eye after hundreds of shops had been looted and tell them we hadn’t lost control,” Nunez said.

Nunez acknowledged a “lack of anticipation” in the deployment of security forces on Saturday, saying their numbers were insufficient to deal with the large crowds of rioters and looters on the fringes of the demonstrations.

He estimated that 60,000 law enforcement personnel were deployed across the country that day.

“Given the damage that has been caused, it was only right that I should hand in my resignation,” Nunez said.

Looting continued on Sunday, and Paris Mayor Emmanuel Gregoire said on Monday that about 30 shops had been targeted in the capital the previous day, describing the scenes as “unbearable”.

Nunez said about 350 people were arrested in Paris on Sunday and overnight.

Nationwide, more than 2,330 people were taken into police custody over the weekend, 70 percent of whom were adults, Justice Minister Gerald Darmanin said.

The violent weekend demonstrations followed weeks of protests by high school students against overcrowded classrooms, teacher shortages and underinvestment in education, the biggest youth-led protest movement in the country in recent memory.

articles.title: Hezbollah funding plan indicates a new challenge to Lebanon’s government
articles.summary: The reported $200m in aid from Iran to Hezbollah has put the Lebanese government under increased pressure from the US.
articles.body:
Beirut, Lebanon – Last week, Hezbollah announced it would provide financial support to families in Lebanon who had lost their homes in the latest war with Israel.

Hezbollah has a long history of providing financial and other support for constituents and compensating those who have lost their homes to Israeli bombing. And while the group has historically received Iranian funding, it also has independent funding pathways allowing it to support members of its base, who are predominantly Lebanese Shia.

But analysts said Hezbollah’s latest distribution drive, announced on October 13, is increasing pressure on the Lebanese government, which has sought to counter the group’s influence in the country.

Last week, the government seized hundreds of kilogrammes of explosives linked to Hezbollah. Hezbollah MP Hassan Fadlallah said the stockpile belongs to the axis of resistance against Israel and demanded that it be handed back and those arrested be released.

Meanwhile, Ali Damoush, the group’s executive council chairman, said on Tuesday Hezbollah would continue to support its constituents who have been on the front lines of the war with Israel.

“At Hezbollah, and out of our religious and moral responsibility, we will continue to serve our people and make every possible effort to preserve their dignity and honour,” he said.

Damoush said the payments were aimed at “displaced people and those whose homes had been destroyed or severely damaged to the point of becoming uninhabitable”.

This follows a report by the Reuters news agency claiming that Iran had provided Hezbollah with $200m in an effort to ease the burden on Lebanon’s Shia population, after three years of devastating war with Israel.

At the height of the war, which began on October 8, 2023, there were as many as 1.2 million people displaced, with about 9,000 Lebanese killed.

A United States Department of State official denied that Iran, under stringent economic pressure, was able to transfer the funds to its Lebanese ally.

Nicholas Blanford, a nonresident senior fellow at the Atlantic Council and author of a book about Hezbollah, told Al Jazeera that the funds would be a huge boon to the group.

“In general, this will help. Hezbollah is very sensitive towards the needs of their support base, the Shia community, and I think that’s one of the reasons why they haven’t gone back to fighting the Israelis,” he said. “The Iranians call the shots ultimately, but for Hezbollah I think there’s an awareness that they need to let their people breathe a little bit.”

Israel intensified its war on Lebanon on March 2 this year, the second such escalation in less than two years.

Hours earlier, Hezbollah had attacked Israel for the first time in more than a year after joint US-Israeli strikes on Tehran killed Iran’s Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, an ally of the group. It also said Israel’s repeated violations of a 2024 ceasefire in southern Lebanon, where Hezbollah has traditionally had a strong presence, were another factor in opening up the war.

In the following days, Israel reinvaded southern Lebanon, displacing more than a million people from their homes and killing about 4,300 since then. Israeli forces began their widespread aerial attacks on Lebanese villages and towns, which they claimed contained Hezbollah positions, with growing intensity.

In June, a US-brokered trilateral framework was agreed between Israel and Lebanon. The goal was to have Israel withdraw from parts of southern Lebanon and have the Lebanese army deployed to disarm Hezbollah. Israel is yet to enter two of the first three pilot zone areas, where this programme was set to be unveiled.

Since then, Israel has largely not withdrawn from the Lebanese territory but has entrenched what analysts believe is likely to become a long-term occupation, with more than 50 front-line villages and towns completely eradicated. Israel continues to demolish houses south of the so-called “Yellow Line” , in a tactic that has mirrored Israeli genocidal actions in Gaza.

Tens of thousands of people remain displaced, staying with relatives, renting apartments, or staying in hotels. Many had their livelihoods disrupted. In this context, Hezbollah has tried to step in and provide support for the displaced, most of whom are Shia Muslims and make up Hezbollah’s support base.

This is where the money from Iran reportedly comes in. However, analysts point out that Hezbollah has its own funding schemes, including financial support from the diaspora. Despite being heavily sanctioned, it is able to access money via domestic financial institutions or cryptocurrency.

“It has access to funds from the state, wealthy individuals, various entities, companies and hospitals,” Marcel Baloukji, a Lebanese political analyst, told Al Jazeera.

Hezbollah says its members have conducted surveys in Beirut’s southern suburbs and in southern Lebanon to assess the damage caused by the war. Families in Beirut and its suburbs whose homes were destroyed in the war will get $14,000 each; those outside the capital will receive $12,000. Financing will also be provided for furniture.

The group said “everyone who has suffered harm in our country, regardless of their political position” will receive support. This suggests that even families who openly criticised the group for plunging the country into a disastrous war with Israel will also be eligible for payments.

“Anyone who owns another home should, in solidarity with us, forgo the housing allowance, but will still receive the furniture allowance,” the group added.

Hezbollah is widely acknowledged as Lebanon’s strongest political and military actor, but the group grew overconfident in the run-up to the October 7, 2023 attacks by Palestinian groups on Israel, analysts say.

The political reality in Lebanon from that point changed, particularly after the 2024 Israeli intensification of its campaign against Hezbollah, which saw much of the group’s military leadership killed, including General Secretary Hassan Nasrallah.

Such a blow has been difficult for the group and its constituents, who have borne much of the brunt of Israel’s assault on Lebanon.

“It’s been a rough three years for them,” Atlantic Council’s Blanford said. “[The funding] will alleviate, to an extent, some people’s suffering.”

Hezbollah’s announcement of support for those affected in the war is viewed by many as an attempt to maintain support on the ground.

“Hezbollah knows that providing financial support and compensation to its on-the-ground population is one way to maintain its mass support,” Dania Arayssi, assistant director at New Lines Institute for Strategy and Policy, told Al Jazeera. “This is especially important because Hezbollah has seen a decline in mass support for it and a rise in mass frustration against this ongoing war.”

But the group’s efforts to pay off those who have suffered do not guarantee loyalty. Many in the Shia community have praised Hezbollah for the support they have received, but most say it is not enough to cover their expenses.

“I’ve been hearing that there may be a problem between those that get compensation for destroyed homes and those with badly damaged homes who are going to get nothing,” Blanford said.

Arayssi said Hezbollah’s latest move will also be a challenge for the Lebanese government, which has come under increasing Israeli and US pressure to take action against Hezbollah’s influence.

Last Thursday, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio phoned Lebanon’s President Joseph Aoun to press him on the issue of the Hezbollah explosives Lebanese forces had confiscated .

“The Lebanese government is facing a real test and challenge to build and win the trust of the international community, and particularly the United States, against Hezbollah’s signalling attempts of rebuilding itself,” Arayssi said.

“This funding and support for Hezbollah will likely make it harder to negotiate with Israel on the verification plan and even on the withdrawal from remaining territories, claiming that the government is failing to control its financial system.”

articles.title: Watch: Russian satellite chases Ukraine-linked spacecraft in space; raises alarm
articles.summary: A Russian military satellite has manoeuvred into close proximity with a commercial radar-imaging satellite linked to Ukraine's military, raising concerns
articles.body: A Russian military satellite has manoeuvred into close proximity with a commercial radar-imaging satellite linked to Ukraine's military, raising concerns that Moscow could be monitoring or potentially interfering with Western space assets.Russia's Kosmos 2612 has adjusted its orbit to match that of ICEYE-X36, a satellite operated by Finland-founded company ICEYE. articles.title: World Food Programme cuts aid to 500,000 Palestinians in Gaza, citing funding shortages
articles.summary: The U.N. World Food Programme has said funding shortages are forcing major cuts to its aid in Gaza, leaving about 500,000 people without monthly food support in a territory where two-thirds of the population struggle to get enough to eat.
articles.body: The U.N. World Food Programme has said funding shortages are forcing major cuts to its aid in Gaza, leaving about 500,000 people without monthly food support in a territory where two-thirds of the population struggle to get enough to eat. The WFP said it was reducing the number of recipients of its monthly assistance to 1.1 million people from 1.6 million. In addition, food rations have been halved, cash assistance has been cut for 75,000 families, and the number of daily hot meals for those unable to cook has fallen to 150,000 from 250,000, with some families in hard-to-reach areas now receiving a hot meal only every other day. The WFP said about 1.4 million people, or two-thirds of Gaza’s population, face crisis levels of food insecurity or worse, including roughly 200,000 people in emergency conditions. Last year’s U.S.-brokered Gaza ceasefire calls for the eventual reconstruction of the territory. But little progress has been made towards implementing a deal to end the conflict that includes terms for Hamas to disarm and Israel to withdraw its troops. “It’s a year into the agreement of this ceasefire. Well, life is still brutal here. There is no proper shelter.. There is no basic services. There is no safety, no security,” acting Executive Director of the World Food Program WFP Carl Skau told Reuters in Gaza. “These cuts are happening just as we are facing the fourth winter. You know, I’ve been through the winters here, absolutely brutal,” he added. The WFP said it urgently needs $450 million over the next six months to maintain critical operations in Gaza and the Israeli-occupied West Bank. “We tell the world now is this is not the time to look away. This is the time to step up to sustain this support, to protect the progress that has been made, but also to push for early recovery,” said Skau.

articles.title: Rubio says there was no US pause in intelligence sharing with Ukraine
articles.summary: Ukraine relies on US intel through Starshield to spot fast-moving ballistic missiles that Russia fires at its cities.
articles.body:
United States Secretary of State Marco Rubio has denied any suspension of intelligence-sharing with Ukraine after President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Washington has resumed providing critical ⁠intelligence to help Kyiv defend against Russian missile strikes.

“There has been no pause,” Rubio told reporters while on a visit to Uzbekistan on Monday. “What [Zelenskyy] should be focused on and what we want to be focused on is bringing an end to this war.”

Ukraine has ⁠relied on US intelligence through Starshield , the military-grade version of the Starlink satellite service, to detect the fast-moving ballistic missiles that Russia has fired in waves at its cities.

Asked about a possible ‌meeting between US President Donald Trump, Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese leader Xi Jinping to negotiate an end to ⁠the more than four-year Ukraine war, ⁠Rubio said: “There’s been talks of a meeting. I don’t know ⁠whether it’s been finalised, but ⁠the president [Trump] ⁠has been clear. He’d like the war in Ukraine and Russia ‌to end.”

The comments were made after Ukrainian officials said some Russian strikes had occurred without warning. Speaking to the NBC TV network’s Meet the Press programme on Sunday, Zelenskyy said intelligence-sharing had been interrupted but was later “deblocked”.

“We are very thankful for this,” he said. “Now it works.”

Zelenskyy also said ‌other US actions, such as signing a deal to import Russian diesel and waiving sanctions on Russia that had been slated to take effect this week, will hurt Ukraine.

“If the United States will officially take the side of Russia, of course if these two countries will be together, of course, we will not prevail, and we will not be able to stand,” he said.

Trump on Sunday defended his decision to waive some sanctions on Russia while accusing Zelenskyy of not wanting to end the war.

“My decision on Russia is a very simple one. I am in the process of negotiating Peace in the war between Russia and Ukraine, and don’t want to do anything that will drive, foolishly, Russia away from the bargaining table,” Trump wrote on his Truth Social platform.

He claimed that “Zelenskyy doesn’t care” about ending the conflict. “Frankly, with all of the money that Europe is famously giving him … he doesn’t want to end this war, and probably never did.”

Trump has temporarily waived sanctions on Russian diesel, allowing large quantities to flow into global markets in a bid to lower fuel prices.

The US president also reiterated his accusation that Ukraine was purposefully targeting Russian refineries to try to hurt Trump’s Republican Party in the November 3 midterm elections.

Polling has suggested Trump’s party is heading for a likely defeat in the elections as many voters are upset by fuel costs, which have soared since the US and Israel launched a war on Iran in late February.

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent spoke with Meet the Press after it ‌aired Zelenskyy’s interview, saying the Ukrainian president “presents a false binary this morning that Ukraine must ‌win”.

“The war must end, and that will be with some kind of a negotiated settlement,” he said.

Bessent slammed the claim that the US government was behind the slowing of the SpaceX satellite communications. “President Trump and Secretary Rubio have categorically said that no one in the Trump administration did that,” he said. “And I think it is very reckless for President Zelenskyy to make such a charge.”

Meanwhile, in Ukraine, a Russian missile attack ⁠killed ⁠a woman and wounded several people in the capital, Kyiv, overnight, Mayor Vitali Klitschko said on Telegram on Monday.

The attack also damaged a metro station, a medical facility, an educational institution and a nonresidential building, according to the State Emergency Service.

articles.title: Qatar warns global energy shockwaves from Iran war have yet to peak
articles.summary: Deputy PM calls for dialogue with Tehran, highlights US defence ties and rejects Strait of Hormuz transit fees.
articles.body:
Doha, Qatar — Qatar’s deputy prime minister has warned that global energy shockwaves from the US-Israel war on Iran have yet to reach their peak, raising concerns about further disruption to supplies, international trade and economic growth.

Speaking at the Global Security Forum in Doha on Monday, Sheikh Saoud bin Abdulrahman Al Thani, who also serves as Minister of State for Defence Affairs, identified several threats facing Qatar and the wider Gulf, including risks to sovereignty and disruptions to energy supplies.

“We haven’t reached the peak with respect to energy,” he said, warning of further repercussions “in the coming days and months”.

His remarks come amid continued instability in the Strait of Hormuz – a vital waterway for global oil and liquefied natural gas (LNG) shipments – following the US-Israeli attacks on Iran on February 28, and Tehran’s retaliatory strikes across the region.

Iranian strikes on Qatar’s Ras Laffan industrial complex in March damaged facilities, with repairs expected to take several years.

“We were surprised,” Al Thani said when asked about the attack, adding that there had since been “a lot of discussion with Iran”.

He said Qatar had drawn lessons from the strikes, “to make sure that all of our assets will be protected from any unexpected attack”.

Al Thani also warned against imposing tolls on ships passing through the Strait of Hormuz.

“Transit fees should not be applied,” he said, adding that uncertainty over the waterway would ultimately affect consumers worldwide.

Despite the attacks, Al Thani said Qatar continued to maintain contact with Tehran.

“We never stop our communication,” he said, adding that the two countries remained in touch at different levels despite their disagreements.

He described Qatar’s relationship with Iran before the attacks as one of trust, pointing to their shared offshore gasfield and longstanding economic interests.

Al Thani expressed hope that mediation efforts involving Qatar, Pakistan and Oman would help produce an agreement between the United States, Iran and other parties, including Israel.

He said a sustainable settlement would require broader regional dialogue involving Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries, Pakistan and Turkiye, in consultation with international allies.

“We need to build this on trust,” he added.

Al Thani also suggested developing economic ties with Iran to prevent future conflicts, citing cooperation between France and Germany following decades of hostilities.

“Iran is our neighbour. We need to find ways to live with them,” he said.

Al Thani also highlighted Qatar’s longstanding defence partnership with Washington, saying that “more than 90 percent” of attacks had been prevented through shared expertise and military capabilities developed over the past three to four decades.

He said Qatar was continuing to develop Al Udeid airbase, which hosts US forces and military personnel from other partner countries.

The base was itself targeted by Iran during the conflict, with Qatar reporting that it had shot down two Iranian warplanes during an attack in early March.

Al Thani also announced plans for a new regional defence partnership, saying Qatar was prioritising several aspects including air defence, counter-drone measures and cybersecurity.

“I’m happy to announce today also that soon we’re going to announce a new partnership,” he said, without naming the regional partners involved.

The deputy prime minister stressed that Qatar’s mediation efforts did not diminish its commitment to defending its territory.

“Mediation doesn’t mean that we should not be ready for any defensive action from our side,” he said.
