articles.title: In 2013, Amanda Seyfried bought a 1930s farm in New York's Catskills; she expanded the house, converted an old barn into a two-bedroom guesthouse and turned the property into a nonprofit animal rescue sanctuary
articles.summary: Amanda Seyfried may be known for her Hollywood roles, but her favourite place to unwind is far removed from red carpets and film sets.
articles.body: Amanda Seyfried may be known for her Hollywood roles, but her favourite place to unwind is far removed from red carpets and film sets. The actor bought a 1930s farm in New York’s Catskills region in 2013 and gradually transformed it into a home for her family and a refuge for rescued animals. In a 2025 profile, Architectural Digest described how Seyfried expanded the original farmhouse, converted a barn into a two-bedroom guesthouse and made the rural property her primary residence. In a separate report, People highlighted her description of the animal rescue farm as her dream, detailing its nonprofit status and the animals she and her family care for.A farmhouse that grew with her lifeSeyfried’s decision to settle in the Catskills was driven by her desire for privacy, nature and a quieter life away from the pressures of Hollywood. She fell in love with the farmhouse’s rustic stonework and a trellis connecting the house to a detached garage, she told The Wall Street Journal, as cited by Architectural Digest.The original house was small, so Seyfried and her family expanded it to add a kitchen. Rather than replacing the property’s older structures, they adapted them to meet their changing needs. The farm gradually became both a family home and a place where rescued animals could live. Her husband, actor Thomas Sadoski, joined her at the Catskills property after the couple married in 2017. The family also includes their two children, born in 2017 and 2020.The farmhouse’s interiors reflect Seyfried’s preference for a relaxed, lived-in atmosphere rather than a formal celebrity home. She worked with designer Sarah Zames of General Assembly to shape the property’s spaces. In a 2024 interview with House Beautiful, she described a cosy window-seat nook in the first-floor living room as her favourite spot, where she could crochet or simply sit and unwind.A two-bedroom guesthouse and animal rescue sanctuaryOne of the most significant changes to the property involved an existing barn. Instead of leaving the structure unused, Seyfried had it converted into a two-bedroom guesthouse. According to Architectural Digest, the renovated space includes a kitchenette, a lounge area and a gym. The transformation allowed the building to serve a new purpose without losing its connection to the farm’s agricultural past. Part of the barn continues to be used for storing hay, while the horses have another barn nearby.The guesthouse is an example of how the property’s existing structures have been adapted rather than discarded. The result is a farm that combines its historic character with the practical requirements of a family home.The farm’s most distinctive feature, however, is its role in animal rescue. In its December 2025 report, People described the property as a 501(c)(3) nonprofit animal rescue farm in upstate New York. The designation refers to a category of US nonprofit organisations that qualify for federal tax-exempt status.The property is home to rescued horses, donkeys, goats, chickens, ducks, cats and dogs. Seyfried has spoken about the challenges and rewards of caring for animals, many of whom are elderly or have medical needs. A local caretaker helps the family manage the daily responsibilities involved in looking after them.The work is not simply about providing space. Animals that have experienced neglect, abandonment or health problems can require regular feeding, specialised care and veterinary attention. Looking after them becomes an ongoing commitment rather than a one-time act of rescue.Seyfried has also spoken about her bond with her pony, Cliff, who was 38 when she discussed him in the interview cited by Architectural Digest. She described the time she still had with him as a gift, reflecting the attachment that can develop between people and animals over many years.For Seyfried, the farm offers a sense of accomplishment that is independent of her professional success. In a 2020 interview with The New York Times, she spoke about how satisfying it was to feel successful at home without needing to be in a successful film. She has also explained that caring for ageing animals helps her focus on immediate responsibilities instead of worrying about things beyond her control. articles.title: Nottingham Forest's Morgan Gibbs-White fined after his car ran red light
articles.summary: The midfielder failed to respond to two police letters asking whether he was driving at the time of the offence.
articles.body:
England and Nottingham Forest attacking midfielder Morgan Gibbs-White has been handed a £1,000 court bill after his Range Rover was caught running a red light.

The 26-year-old's vehicle was caught on camera going past a set of lights in West Bridgford, Nottinghamshire, 1.1 seconds after they turned red.

Gibbs-White, who earned his first England cap in 2024, failed to respond to two police letters asking him to confirm if he had been driving at the time of the red light offence, according to court documents.

Last Tuesday, he was convicted by a court of failing to provide the identity of a driver at the time of an offence.

Nottinghamshire Police put out an alert on Gibbs-White's car when the force tried to investigate the traffic light incident, and found the number plate registered with the DVLA was one letter different from what was on the vehicle.

Staffordshire Police then pulled over the Range Rover in April and confirmed it belonged to Gibbs-White.

At Southern Derbyshire Magistrates' Court, he was fined £660, given six penalty points on his licence and ordered to pay £120 in costs and a £264 victim surcharge.

A court official said Gibbs-White did not enter a plea or mitigation, and was sentenced behind closed doors under the fast-track Single Justice Procedure.

Court papers show a Nottinghamshire Police camera caught Gibbs-White's car going past a red traffic light at 15:17 GMT on 28 January in Radcliffe Road.

"At the time of the offence, the vehicle was captured failing to comply with a red light signal, the time into the red light was recorded as 1.1 seconds," a police worker wrote in her statement.

Gibbs-White was banned from driving for six months in May last year after he was caught speeding six times in the space of three months.

At the time, he was ordered to pay just under £4,000 in fines for the spate of offences, including two speeding tickets acquired on the same day.

Gibbs-White, who signed for Forest in 2022 from Wolverhampton Wanderers, has made 10 appearances for England and was called up to Thomas Tuchel's recent squad for the Nations League.

articles.title: HC sets aside Goonda Act detention, says public order claims need evidence
articles.summary: Karnataka HC quashes Goonda Act detention of Bagalkot man, says public order claims need evidence; preventive detention can’t replace bail cancellation.
articles.body: Bengaluru: Merely stating that a person’s activities are prejudicial to public order, without supporting material, is not sufficient to justify preventive detention under the Goonda Act, the Karnataka High Court has held while ordering the release of a man from Bagalkot district.A division bench of Justices M Nagaprasanna and Hema Kulkarni allowed a habeas corpus petition filed by Kavitha, wife of Sanju Vitthal Kadkol, a resident of Jamakhandi. Kadkol was detained under the Karnataka Prevention of Dangerous Activities of Bootleggers, Drug Offenders, Gamblers, Goondas, Immoral Traffic Offenders, Slum Grabbers, and Video or Audio Pirates Act, 1985.The detention order was passed on July 6 and subsequently confirmed, including by the advisory board. Challenging his continued detention, Kavitha contended that her husband was being held illegally.Opposing the petition, the govt advocate submitted that Kadkol was a habitual offender who repeatedly indulged in the illegal use of weapons and faced charges under the Arms Act, 1959. The court was also told that copies of the documents relied upon by the authorities had been furnished to him and that the advisory board had rejected his plea for release.However, examining the records, the bench noted that Kadkol had been acquitted in one of the four criminal cases against him and was out on bail in the other three, where trials were pending.Citing several Supreme Court judgments, the bench observed that preventive detention could not be used as a substitute for seeking cancellation of bail. It also reiterated the distinction between a threat to public order and a mere breach of law and order, noting that preventive detention requires the former.The state had cited Kadkol’s inclusion in the rowdy sheet, his history and alleged gang activities, illegal sources of income, the fear he had allegedly created among the public and intimidation of witnesses.The bench, however, pointed out that the state had neither sought cancellation of bail in the pending cases nor challenged the acquittal. It also noted that no non-bailable warrant had been issued against Kadkol for violating bail conditions or failing to attend court proceedings.Holding that the material on record did not justify preventive detention, the bench allowed the petition and ordered Kadkol’s release.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Bengaluru | Silver Rate in Bengaluru | Bank Holidays in Bengaluru | Public Holidays in Bengaluru | Bengaluru AQI | Weather in Bengaluru | Petrol Price in Bengaluru | Diesel Price in Bengaluru | CNG Price in Bengaluru | LPG Price in BengaluruStay updated with the latest Bengaluru news. articles.title: At least 18 killed in Houthi attack on military camp in Yemen’s Shabwa
articles.summary: Houthis launch ballistic missiles at camp in southern governorate during training exercise, gov’t forces spokesman says.
articles.body:
Dozens of people have been killed and wounded in a Houthi missile attack on the al-AIam military camp in southern Yemen, authorities say.

The Houthis launched three ballistic missiles on Monday at the camp in Shabwa governorate during a training exercise, a spokesperson for the Yemeni government forces said.

Officials in the internationally recognised government and medical sources said at least 18 people were killed and more than 30 wounded in the attack. The deputy governor of Shabwa said there were at least 40 casualties without giving a breakdown of those killed and injured.

The attack was carried out as fighting continued to rage across Yemen. The civil war has escalated sharply since the Houthis, an armed group also known as Ansar Allah (Arabic for Supporters of God), seized strategic territory from forces loyal to the government along the Red Sea coast last month.

Government forces, backed by Saudi Arabia, responded to the losses with a counteroffensive and then launched the “Dawn of Yemen” operation, which aims to recapture Houthi-held territory, including the capital, Sanaa, which the Iran-aligned group seized in 2014.

Rashad al-Alimi, the head of the Yemeni Presidential Leadership Council, said those killed were new recruits and promised a “firm response”.

“Targeting recruits reflects the Houthi militia’s approach of resorting to terrorist attacks when under pressure,” he said.

Reporting from Sanaa, Al Jazeera’s Yousef Mawry said the Houthis claimed responsibility for the attack.

“The Houthis said the attack targeted what they called a ‘Saudi-backed’ military base, referring to Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces who are stationed at military camps across the country,” he said.

“The Houthis say they will continue to target those bases. Spokesperson Yahya Saree says anywhere with a Saudi-backed military presence will be considered a legitimate target.”

Earlier, Yemeni government forces said they targeted Houthi gatherings, vehicles and weapons in al-Aqroudh, al-Shaqab and al-Sarari, south of Taiz, which is suffering from fuel shortages and soaring prices.
